import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()

    # Sort by user_id, event_ts, event_id (ordering rule)
    events = events.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"],
        kind="mergesort",
        ignore_index=True
    )

    # Calendar date (server local, assumed naive timestamps)
    events["event_date"] = events["event_ts"].dt.date

    # Identify previous user / ts / date within the same user group
    prev_user = events["user_id"].shift(1)
    prev_ts = events["event_ts"].shift(1)
    prev_date = events["event_date"].shift(1)

    is_new_user = events["user_id"] != prev_user

    # Gap in minutes from previous event (NaT-safe)
    gap_minutes = (events["event_ts"] - prev_ts).dt.total_seconds() / 60.0

    different_date = events["event_date"] != prev_date
    gap_exceeded = gap_minutes > 45

    new_session = is_new_user | different_date | gap_exceeded

    # session_num resets per user: cumulative count of new_session flags within each user
    events["session_num"] = new_session.groupby(events["user_id"]).cumsum().astype("int64")

    # Aggregate
    user_sessions = events.groupby(
        ["user_id", "session_num"],
        as_index=False
    ).agg(
        session_date=("event_date", "first"),
        session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
        session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
        event_count=("event_id", "count")
    )

    user_sessions = user_sessions.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "session_num"],
        ignore_index=True
    )

    user_sessions = user_sessions[
        ["user_id", "session_num", "session_date", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]
    ]

    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
